en: the loving Mother, as she saw
the sufferings of her glorious Son.
Who is the man who would not weep
if he saw the Mother of Christ
to behold the Mother of Christ
For the sins of his people
as he gave up his spirit.
make me feel the force of sorrow,
so that I may mourn with you.
fix the wounds of the crucified one
who deigned so much to suffer for me,
Make me weep devoutly with you,
as long as I shall live.
To stand beside the cross with you,
and to join myself to you
be not now bitter to me:
Make me bear the death of Christ,
make me a sharer of his passion,
and dwell again on his wounds.
Make me be wounded with his wounds,
make me be made drunk with the cross
and with the blood of the Son.
Lest I burn, set aflame by fire,
through you, Virgin, may I be defended
Christ, when it is time to go hence,
grant that through your mother I may come
grant that to the soul be given
notes: 16.3: 'plagas recolere' is literally 'to go over again / call to mind again the wounds'.
17.2: 'cruce inebriari' is literally 'to be made drunk with the cross'.
19.3: the palm is the sign of victory (of the martyrs).
lines 9.2-9.3: the verb "fac" (make) stands at the start of 9.3 in the Latin; the English moves it up.
